text: Sunlight is every color. So why does the sky choose blue?
The answer is the air. It is full of tiny gas molecules.
When sunlight hits them, the molecules bounce it in new directions.
But they bounce blue light about five times more than red.
Blue gets scattered all across the sky.
So wherever you look up, blue light is coming at you.
At sunset, the light crosses much more air to reach you.
Along the way, most of the blue gets bounced aside.
Only the reds and oranges are left.
The sky doesn't choose blue. The air scatters it to you.
